participants.note: suggested custom C++20 rewrite instead of GSL and raised constructor selection ambiguity; approved head commit
raised concern on template verbosity at call sites and requested aliases; approved earlier iterations

claims.harm: repeating verbose template instantiations for non-null smart pointers makes call sites hard to read and adopt
claims.quote: Could we avoid repeating the verbose template instantiation for all non-null smart pointers? I like the extra guarantee, but I don't like how verbose the results are.

claims.harm: carrying a customized third-party GSL base introduces unnecessary complexity and maintenance burden
claims.quote: I'm not sure using gsl as a base makes sense for us. It seems very unlikely that this will ever be standardized, and we're already customizing it here quite a bit already. It seems like we don't care about the strict_not_null vs not_null separation, so we might as well avoid the complexity altogether?
claims.settled_by_quote: it makes sense to just write a minimal, clean, and C++20 impl ourselves. So I went over all lines in your branch, applied some small test fixups, and then pushed it here.

claims.harm: direct-initialization of non-const lvalues selects the forwarding constructor over the copy constructor, triggering an unnecessary assertion and divergence on moved-from objects
claims.quote: For a non-const lvalue NotNull<T> under direct-init, the forwarding ctor is selected instead of the copy ctor.

support.reason: Concept ACK, I think this could help in a few cases where the pointer-like type is part of the contract and a plain reference would not preserve the ownership/storage semantics.
